definition.scope: Every number is counted from the live rows in this system's database. In this demo those rows include records made by the seed script and by simulated-clock runs, so the figures describe this deployment, not AICTE's real caseload.
definition.window: The From and To dates (inclusive; all dates if none given) apply to the date each alert was logged, on the system's SIMULATED clock (the date the demo is pretending it is), not the real calendar date. The same window applies to total, byKind, reminderTiming, perDay and escalationsByLevel. The notifications block is NOT windowed: it always describes every notification ever created.
definition.total: Number of alerts the deadline engine logged in the window: one row per deadline item, kind and level (daily digests are one row per user per day, not per item), so the same alert is never logged twice. Blank (null) when no engine run and no alert has ever been recorded (engineEverRan is true if either exists, even an alert with no run on file), meaning "none recorded". Otherwise the engine has recorded activity at some time (not necessarily in this window). A total of 0 means no alert was logged in this window. This counts the decision to alert. This build has no external delivery channel, so it says nothing about an alert reaching anyone outside the system.
definition.byKind: Alerts in the window counted by kind (REMINDER, AT_RISK, OVERDUE, ESCALATION, DIGEST). The counts add up to total.
definition.reminderTiming: Timeliness of REMINDER alerts only. reminders = reminder alerts in the window; late = reminders raised more than one day after their reminder date, which has two causes the log cannot tell apart (the deadline engine had not run in time, or the deadline item was created after that reminder date had already passed, for example an item due in 5 days has already missed its 30-day and 15-day reminder dates), so late does not by itself mean the engine was slow; onTime = reminders - late, so onTime + late = reminders (not total). The other alert kinds (at-risk, overdue, escalation, digest) have no timeliness measure in this system, so they are not counted as on time or late. Blank when total is blank.
definition.perDay: Alerts per simulated calendar day, only for days on which at least one alert was logged; days with none are left out, never shown as zero, and nothing is back-filled. The simulated date in this demo can be moved forward, and alerts are only logged when the engine runs, so a missing day usually means the engine did not run on that date, not that no alerts were due. perDay therefore records when the engine ran and is not an operational trend: do not read a rising or falling line as the workload getting better or worse. The counts add up to total.
definition.escalationsByLevel: Escalation alerts in the window counted by escalation level (1, 2 or 3, raised as a deadline item becomes more overdue). Only levels with at least one alert are listed. The counts add up to the escalation kind in byKind.
definition.notifications: Every in-system notification ever created (not windowed): total, read (opened by its recipient) and unread = total - read. informative is true only when read is above 0. While nobody has opened any notification, "0 read" is a true count but says nothing about whether people see alerts, so it should not be presented as a result.
definition.notRecorded: Acknowledgement (someone confirming they have seen an alert) is not recorded: a notification has a read flag but no timestamp, and no alert is tied to a person who confirmed it, so no figure for it exists here. It is listed so its absence is visible rather than mistaken for zero.
definition.notComputed: Time from an alert to its deadline item closing IS recorded per item (the item's closedAt, stamped with the system clock when the item is closed; AlertLog.itemId links each alert to its item), but this page does not compute or chart it. An item that is still open has no closedAt, so it has no such time, and closing an item does not show that the alert prompted anyone to act. Exception flags also carry raised and resolved timestamps, but they are separate from alerts.

notComputed: time from alert to deadline item closing
